text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- All taxpayers holding property worth over 50,000 zlotys will have to declare it in their tax returns, a new tax ordinance bill produced by parliamentary committees said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Wroclaw province economic court has declared bankrupt the Odra shoemaker in Olesnica, south-western Poland. The plant's debt is now 16 million zlotys.
- Bank Handlowy subsidiary Handlowy Investments will form a joint venture real estate fund with the Pioneer investment trust. The new fund's capital will initially be $60 million.
- Soft commodity options for maize, pork bellies, quarters of beef, wheat and rye will be issued this month on the Warsaw Commodity Exchange.
- Licence fees to be paid by insurance brokers are excessive, according to the finance ministry's insurance and tax departments, the insurance department's director Anatol Adamski said.

- The Bauma construction firm's 1.2 million C-series shares, which were priced at 10 zlotys per share in a public offer in January, will be listed for public trading on the Warsaw bourse on May 21, the company said.
- The Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank will be the official sponsor of Pope John Paul II's visit to Poland this month, the bank said.
- Sogelease, leasing subsidiary of France's Societe Generale, has opened a Polish subsidiary, Sogelease said.
- The Polish Private Equity Fund 1 and 2, administered by Enterprise Investors, will buy a 28 percent stake in a new $15 million new share issue by the Lukas leasing firm.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI -
The Lukas leasing firm launched an internet credit service yesterday, Lukas' president Mariusz Lukasiewicz said.
- New import duties on starch were introduced as of today and the agriculture ministry is mulling reintroduction of a 20 percent duty on grain imports, Agriculture Minister Jacek Kalinowski said.
- Economic data from 1996 show that despite a growth rate decline Poland's economy is in a phase of intensive development, a report by the strategic studies and development institute (IRISS) said.

- As of May 21 brokerage houses will have to submit preliminary annual reports and consolidated reports to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW), a new regulation says. Hitherto, brokerages had only to produce monthly, six month and annual financial reports.

- The Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environmental protection bank is considering the purchase of the Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank in Lublin, eastern Poland. BOS has given up its plan to buy Bank Pocztowy postal bank as Pocztowy is not interested in a strategic investor.
- HSBC Guziejewski and Albrecht brokerage house will develop its service offer addressed to institutional investors, the brokerage's president Pawel Guziejewski said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Over 17,000 flats were completed by the end of April showing a 10 percent upturn compared with the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
PARKIET
- Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich has issued two-year zloty bonds worth 100 million zlotys.
- The Gdansk provincial court has announced the bankruptcy of the Bacutil fodder plant, controlled by the Fortuna National Investment Fund (NFI) No.13.
Reuters has not verified the above stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
